chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani, from Musa ibn Muhammad al-Ijli, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, raising it (as a marfu' narration), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
'They belied Our Signs, all of them'
— meaning the Successors (Awsiya), all of them.

key_terms.آياتنا: Our Signs — interpreted here as the Imams, the divinely appointed legatees
key_terms.الأوصياء: The Awsiya (Successors/Legatees) — the Imams who succeed the Prophet as guardians of the faith
key_terms.رفعه: Marfu' — a hadith transmission term indicating the chain is raised to an infallible source without complete enumeration of all intermediate narrators

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about 'Our Signs' in Quran 54:42?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets Quran 54:42 — 'They belied Our Signs, all of them' — as referring to the divine appointment of all the Imams (Awsiya, successors). The Imam teaches that the 'Signs' (ayat) of Allah mentioned in this verse are the divinely designated legatees from the Prophet's lineage, and that rejecting any one of them constitutes a rejection of all. This hadith is part of the 'Chapter on the Signs which Allah Mentioned in His Book, they are the Imams,' establishing the theological basis for the imamate as a Quranic institution.
